_doc: THE single source of truth for model selection — read by Python (bob_models.py). Converted from the retired config/models.psd1; full field prose is in that file's git history. Per-model schema: repo/path=HuggingFace repo+file -> download URL; gguf=local filename in models/ (also the -m runtime path); ctx=context window (-c). ALWAYS set it, embedders and rerankers included: with no -c llama-server reserves the model's full trained window, which measured 4.8 GB for the 0.6B embedder and 5.7 GB for the 0.6B reranker versus 1.4 GB each at -c 2048; sizeGB=approx on-disk size; kv=true applies the KV-cache quant macro; flags=extra llama-server flags (appended last, so they override srv-macro defaults); ngl="auto" drops -ngl so llama.cpp fits the offload to free VRAM itself (needed for a DENSE model bigger than the card, where --n-cpu-moe does not apply); setParams=server-side sampling enforcement, the ONLY place per-role sampling goes (temperature/top_p/top_k/min_p inside flags would be a client-overridable server default, and `bob gen` warns on one); kvQuantK/kvQuantV override the profile-wide KV quant for one model (a long-context model held entirely in VRAM can only afford q4_0); aliasOf="<role>" makes this role a second NAME for that model rather than a second model — it inherits the target's whole spec, downloads once, loads once, and is emitted under llama-swap `aliases:` with its own setParams routed through setParamsByID; ttl=0 never auto-unloads; pinned=true keeps resident (excluded from the swap group); embedding adds --embedding. Keys starting with '_' are METADATA (e.g. _targetVRAM, _notes, _cpuTier), not models — skipped by the generator and downloader. activeProfile here is the shipped DEFAULT; the writable override lives in data/active-profile.json (bob profile) and env BOB_PROFILE wins for one invocation. Tunable knobs (defaults block) are overridable per-machine in config/user.json (deep-merged). Re-run `bob gen` after editing.

prompts.coder: You are a skilled software engineer. Be direct. No preambles.
prompts.ponder: Think the problem through before answering: state your assumptions, weigh the alternatives, then give a clear conclusion.
prompts.vision: You are a vision assistant. Describe images concisely and answer questions about them directly.
prompts.writer: You are a careful writer. Plan the structure before drafting, then produce clear, well-organized prose. No preambles.

deepseek._capacity: contextWindow/maxOutputTokens are the models' limits, set on the peer or overridden per role. maxOutputTokens is the output cap every *-pro route defaults to (litellm.yaml max_tokens, and the dsh route); a client that sends its own max_tokens still wins. V4 flash and pro take 1M in and far more than 32K out. supportsVision marks a role image capable, and neither V4 model takes images.

zhipu._capacity: GLM-5 family: 200000 in and 128000 out on every host LiteLLM lists; both are stated at the conservative end.

kimi._capacity: kimi-k3 limits unconfirmed: set contextWindow and maxOutputTokens before enabling, or the provider's default output cap applies.

16gb._targetVRAM: 16GB (tested RTX 5080 / RTX 5060 Ti) — every role but vision on one resident model
16gb._notes: One Qwen3.8-27B GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS (10.09 GB) serves chat/coder/ponder/writer/agent, fully on the card: no expert offload, no dense spill. MEASURED on a 16 GB RTX 5080 with a running desktop — chat 10950 MiB at 40960 ctx / q4_0 KV, embed 1198, rerank 1198 (a -c 2048 -ub 128 measurement; the current rerank settings are unmeasured), so Bob holds 13.3 GB and leaves ~0.9 GB beside a ~2 GB compositor. Three things buy that: -c on the 0.6B helpers (with none they reserve their full 32K window — 4.8 GB and 5.7 GB), -ub 128 on the embedder (~226 MiB), and -np 1 (llama-server defaults to four slots, each with its own KV and, on this hybrid attention/SSM model, its own recurrent-state cache). fim joins the swap group here: a resident FIM model does not fit next to a 10 GB chat model, so IDE autocomplete and chat take turns. The -mtp build of the same model is the speed profile (+40% tok/s) but costs ~900 MiB more, which this tier does not have. rerank runs at -c 1024 with -ub 1024 -b 1024, since a rank-pooling reranker rejects any query+document pair longer than its ubatch. A smaller KV partly offsets the larger compute buffer; the net VRAM needs on-card measurement. Sampling is enforced per role with setParams (same values on every tier): ponder 0.3, writer 0.6/0.95, agent 0.1, and coder takes the Qwen3.8 chat setting (1.0/0.95/top_k 20/min_p 0), since the registry records no coder-specific guidance. chat itself uses the Qwen3.8 thinking setting.

24gb._notes: Qwen3.8-27B GSQ-RCO IQ3_S-mtp (12.12 GB, task-lossless vs BF16) plus its 0.93 GB vision projector serves chat/coder/ponder/writer/agent/vision at 98304 ctx with q8_0 KV. ~22.5 GB of the ~23.9 GB free, pinned fim 3B + embed included. rerank runs at -c 1024 with -ub 1024 -b 1024, since a rank-pooling reranker rejects any query+document pair longer than its ubatch. A smaller KV partly offsets the larger compute buffer; the net VRAM needs on-card measurement. Sampling is enforced per role with setParams (same values on every tier): ponder 0.3, writer 0.6/0.95, agent 0.1, and coder takes the Qwen3.8 chat setting (1.0/0.95/top_k 20/min_p 0), since the registry records no coder-specific guidance. chat itself uses the Qwen3.8 thinking setting.
24gb._targetVRAM: ~24GB (RTX 3090 / 4090 / 4080 Super) — one resident model for every chat role

8gb._targetVRAM: ~8GB (ctx 4096, agent 8192, smaller quants): NEEDS on-card validation
8gb._notes: A 27B build does not fit: the 8.4 GB IQ2_XS weights leave no room for context. writer rides ponder (same 9B gguf) rather than loading it twice. rerank runs at -c 1024 with -ub 1024 -b 1024, since a rank-pooling reranker rejects any query+document pair longer than its ubatch. A smaller KV partly offsets the larger compute buffer; the net VRAM needs on-card measurement. Sampling is enforced per role with setParams (same values on every tier): ponder 0.3, writer 0.6/0.95, agent 0.1, and coder takes the Qwen3.8 chat setting (1.0/0.95/top_k 20/min_p 0), since the registry records no coder-specific guidance. chat samples at 0.7/0.9, the setting this tier's Qwen3.5 chat model ships with, rather than the Qwen3.8 thinking setting the 27B tiers use.

32gb._notes: Same task-lossless IQ3_S-mtp build as 24gb, but --parallel 2 --no-kv-unified splits 393216 ctx into two private 192K slots, so a second agent session costs a KV slot instead of a second card. q4_0 KV to pay for the range. rerank runs at -c 1024 with -ub 1024 -b 1024, since a rank-pooling reranker rejects any query+document pair longer than its ubatch. A smaller KV partly offsets the larger compute buffer; the net VRAM needs on-card measurement. Sampling is enforced per role with setParams (same values on every tier): ponder 0.3, writer 0.6/0.95, agent 0.1, and coder takes the Qwen3.8 chat setting (1.0/0.95/top_k 20/min_p 0), since the registry records no coder-specific guidance. chat itself uses the Qwen3.8 thinking setting.
32gb._targetVRAM: ~32GB (RTX 5090 / A6000) — one resident model, two independent agent slots

12gb._targetVRAM: ~12GB (smaller quants; chat and coder ctx 16384, ponder 8192): NEEDS on-card validation
12gb._notes: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B + Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with expert offload; writer rides ponder and agent rides chat, so the tier holds three GGUFs instead of five. A Qwen3.8-27B GSQ-RCO build only fits here at IQ2_XS once the pinned fim/embed are counted, which costs more code quality than the offloaded MoE pair. rerank runs at -c 1024 with -ub 1024 -b 1024, since a rank-pooling reranker rejects any query+document pair longer than its ubatch. A smaller KV partly offsets the larger compute buffer; the net VRAM needs on-card measurement. Sampling is enforced per role with setParams (same values on every tier): ponder 0.3, writer 0.6/0.95, agent 0.1, and coder takes the Qwen3.8 chat setting (1.0/0.95/top_k 20/min_p 0), since the registry records no coder-specific guidance. chat samples at 0.7/0.9, the setting this tier's Qwen3.5 chat model ships with, rather than the Qwen3.8 thinking setting the 27B tiers use.

cpu._targetVRAM: CPU-only (no GPU) — tiny model, correctness/wiring only, not performance
cpu._notes: One Qwen3.5-0.8B serves chat, writer and agent (writer and agent are aliases, so one server loads). No coder, ponder, vision, fim, embed or rerank: routing falls back to chat for coder/ponder/writer/agent, vision requests are refused, and memory recall runs without embeddings. Sampling is enforced per role with setParams (same values on every tier): ponder 0.3, writer 0.6/0.95, agent 0.1,. chat samples at 0.7/0.9 like the other Qwen3.5 tiers.
